messages:
Alex P.: Heads-up — customer X asked for a single ‘Optimize Advisor’ endpoint that returns batching + cache + quant recommendations and an estimated cost delta. They want per-route guidance and a confidence score.
Priya K.: +1 from product. Need to decide what the API surface looks like and what we guarantee vs advisory.
Mike L.: engineering: we can return a small set of actions (e.g., enable_prefix_cache, target_batch_size=32, quant_profile=q4_0) and an estimated tokens/saved and expected p50 impact. estimating cost delta is doable but noisy.
Jess R.: ops note: for Dedicated customers, advisors must include whether a recommendation requires config changes (autoscale, pooling) or just runtime flags. Different SLAs.
Sam T.: sales-bot posted: "Customer X: willing to pilot if we can show >=20% token cost reduction without >10% p50 increase".
Alex P.: Ok — launch criteria proposal: 1) recommendations pass in-house evals on 3 sample workloads showing median cost reduction >=15% and p50 latency <= +12% 2) API returns explainability text + confidence score 3) UI/Console shows per-route econ impact & action buttons.
Priya K.: scope negotiation: MVP should be read-only advisor (no auto-apply). That avoids infra risk and makes partner trust easier. Agree?
Mike L.: agree. MVP engine: heuristic + lightweight ML model that maps seqlen distro + model variant -> batch size & cache rules. Quant suggestions can be limited to vetted profiles per model family.
Jess R.: we should list edge cases: multi-turn chats with tool calling (KV cache semantics), streams (can't batch across streaming sessions), and re-ranking workloads. Those need special handling.
Maria S.: from eng-ml: eval-triggered alerts: we can tie recommendations to eval regressions — i.e., if a eval suite shows quality drop when quantized, surface an alert and block that quant suggestion.
Sam T.: can we include an "estimated monthly $ impact" in the Console? customers love the $$ number.
Mike L.: yes, but add a big caveat label: estimates assume current traffic and model version. We'll compute = tokens_saved * price_per_token (from account).
Priya K.: UX question: do we make accept/apply buttons per-recommendation in Console, or offer a single batch apply? Which is less risky?
Alex P.: propose per-route accept with a dry-run mode that shows predicted perf using recent traces. Dry-run impl is medium effort but strong value.
Jess R.: risk checklist: audit logging for who applied what, rollback button, canary rollout to 5% of traffic, and rate-limited apply jobs.
Maria S.: metrics we'll publish in the advisor: predicted_token_savings, predicted_cost_delta, expected_p50_change, confidence. Also a short rationale string (e.g., "short seqlen -> increase batch to 24; prefix cache hits 12% currently").
Sam T.: customer asks also included a programmatic hook: POST /advisor/apply-preview that returns a synthetic perf summary. good to support in API v1.
Mike L.: technical note: generating synthetic perf needs trace replays which are heavy; initial preview can be a sim using sequence length hist & kernel benchmarks.
Priya K.: prioritization: rank features for Q2 MVP: 1) Advisor API read-only + Console UI 2) Eval safety checks for quant suggestions 3) Acceptance flows + audit logs 4) Dry-run simulations 5) Auto-apply (TBD).
Alex P.: ask from customers: SLA for recommendation freshness (24h) and ability to pin model variants so advisor respects pinned versions. Add to acceptance criteria.
Jess R.: compliance ask: store only aggregated econ estimates, never raw prompt content unless customer opts in.
Maria S.: action items: Mike/Eng to draft API schema + cost-estimate math by Tue, Product (Priya) to draft acceptance criteria doc, Ops (Jess) to draft rollout & rollback playbook, Sales (Sam) to collect top 3 customer pilot candidates.
Alex P.: cool — let's sync Thu 10am for final scope cut. :thumbsup:
Priya K.: noted. I'll drop docs links in #product-resources after this thread.
Sam T.: pinging sales-bot for pilot list.
sales-bot: pilot candidates posted: Customer X, Customer Y, Customer Z (DM for details). :robot_face:
